title: hyperPad vs Scratch vs GDevelop
summary: Compare hyperPad, Scratch, and GDevelop using current visual-coding, device, free-tier, and publishing information. See why hyperPad is the best fit for...
body_markdown:
*Reviewed October 7, 2026. Scratch information refers to its[official About page](https://scratch.mit.edu/help/about/) . GDevelop information refers to its[current pricing page](https://gdevelop.io/en-gb/pricing) . Plans and publishing limits can change.*


If your goal is to create a complete 2D game through visual logic on iPad, **hyperPad is the option to take** . Scratch is excellent for learning with blocks. GDevelop offers a cross-platform event system and tiered cloud services. hyperPad brings the editor, Scenes, Objects, Behaviors, assets, testing, community feedback, and an iOS export path into one iPad-first workflow.


The paid hyperPad app is also available through the App Store on compatible Apple-silicon Macs, including M1 and later. The App Store listing provides current compatibility details for each device.


## hyperPad vs Scratch vs GDevelop


Decision factor hyperPad Scratch GDevelop


Best fit **Complete visual 2D games on iPad** Introductory creative coding Cross-platform projects


Logic **Connected visual Behaviors** Programming blocks Event system


Creation workflow **Native iPad-first game editor; compatible Apple-silicon Mac access** Learning and remixing environment Desktop, web, and mobile options


Game systems **Scenes, Objects, Attributes, physics, UI, audio, animation, particles, shaders, and Prefabs** Sprites, backdrops, sounds, and blocks Scenes, Objects, events, and extensions


Testing loop **Run, adjust, and retest the Project in the editor** Run and remix projects Preview through its available editors


Community path **Hub sharing, Forum discussion, and creator feedback** Scratch community and remixing GDevelop community and services


Start **Free, ad-free Starter with one editable Project** Free Free and paid service tiers


Why choose it **One visual workflow from first mechanic to an exported iOS game** Learn foundational coding ideas Build for a broader cross-platform workflow


## Why hyperPad is the practical visual game engine


hyperPad teaches the same programming ideas that make visual tools valuable: events, actions, conditions, loops, values, input, state, and debugging. It then connects those ideas to a fuller production system.


A Project can include Scenes, overlays, physics, collisions, UI, animation, particles, shaders, audio, arrays, dictionaries, Prefabs, controller input, and networking. Import your own graphics, fonts, music, and sound effects instead of being restricted to a fixed asset library.


The[Behavior Interface Overview](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/behavior-interface-overview) explains the editor. The[Prefabs and Templates guide](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/prefabs-and-templates) shows how reusable Objects and logic can work across Scenes.


## Why hyperPad is the next step after introductory blocks


Scratch introduces events, sequences, loops, conditions, and variables through blocks. hyperPad carries those ideas into complete 2D game production. A learner can apply the same logic to physics, collisions, UI, custom assets, multiple Scenes, saved state, and reusable game systems on iPad.


## Why hyperPad stands out among visual engines


GDevelop uses event-based logic across a broader cross-platform workflow. hyperPad’s advantage for Apple-device creators is focus: a native, touch-first editor for building, testing, sharing, and expanding visual 2D games directly on iPad, with compatible Apple-silicon Mac access through the App Store.


## What you can build in hyperPad


Start with a one-Scene game:


1. Add a player, obstacle, and collectable as Objects.
2. Connect touch, keyboard, or controller input.
3. Store score and health in Attributes.
4. Add collision events and feedback.
5. Build a win, lose, and restart state.
6. Test immediately, then share through the Hub after upgrading.


That small loop uses real game systems without requiring typed syntax.


## Why the Apple-device workflow matters


On iPad, hyperPad supports touch, Apple Pencil, keyboard, mouse, and trackpad use. On a compatible M1-or-later Mac, the same App Store app can support a larger-screen workflow. You do not have to translate a classroom lesson or prototype between unrelated editors.


Choose the workflow that fits the Project you want to finish. Test one representative mechanic before committing to a larger build, then judge the tool by how clearly you can create, test, and revise it.


For an iPad owner who wants to move from visual coding concepts to a complete playable 2D game, **hyperPad is the best fit of these three** .


Continue with[How to Use hyperPad](https://www.hyperpad.com/blog/how-to-use-hyperpad) or open the[OrbitRun beginner tutorial](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/build-orbitrun-with-smart-shape-part-1-your-first-launch) .
